RHINO WHISPERER

By: Tarryn Crossman | Commission

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
When poachers wiped out most of the herd, Justine Terblanche couldn’t just watch from the sidelines. So he moved into the bush, living among the last surviving rhinos to earn their trust and protect them. Jutsin doesn't see himself as a hero, just a man who couldn't walk away.

Further information:
The Rhino Whisperer

Synopsis:
Just a few years ago, this farm was home to nineteen wild rhinos. Now, only four remain — Amanda, Brittany, Tiffany, and a curious little calf named Herbie. The others? Lost to poachers.
For 27-year-old Justine Terblanche, that loss wasn’t something he could just stand by and watch. He started here as a guard, walking 12-hour shifts with a rifle and a flashlight. But the killing didn’t stop. And something inside him shifted. He knew he had to do more, to be more, if these rhinos had any chance.
So, he moved into the bush.
For eight months, Justine lived alongside the rhinos. He slept under the stars, letting his hair grow so they’d recognise his scent, learning their sounds and copying their movements. It wasn’t some romantic idea — it was survival. He was thrown, trampled, and bruised more than once. But in time, something remarkable happened: they let him in. Now, these wild animals trust him. They come when he calls. They let him touch them.

But the danger hasn’t gone. The poachers are still out there. The farm has fenced off 50 hectares of bush, creating safer zones. Justine moves the rhinos between camps using only a whistle. One call, and they come.
This is a window into Justine Terblanche's world, he doesn’t see himself as a hero, just a man who couldn’t walk away. We’ll spend a day and night with him walking the fence lines, tracking prints in the dust, and witnessing the quiet bond between a man and the last of his herd.

Script:


(Justin) I'm from Citrus Town called Patensie. We grew up without a television in the home and I feel that was a blessing, because then I was outside all the time. And that's where life is.
(Justin up sound talking to his dog subtitles)

(Justin) For a long period of time I got sucked into a normal civilized life. I was married, I had a home in town, all those kinds of things. I never liked that, but I had to do it, because that's what everyone just does.

(Justin) But, when I started to work here, I started to feel like the normal life in town, it's clashing with what's going on over here. And what I wanted more was this.
(Govan voice over) 27-year-old Justin Terblanche isn’t the kind of ranger who clocks off at sunset. He’s taken a radical, some might say unorthodox, approach to his job as a member of this reserves anti-poaching unit.
(Justin) I saw myself as just the guard protecting the rhinos, just doing my duties. But because I lost a rhino due to sickness, we couldn't get close to them. I want to make sure that I can protect them security-wise against poaching, but also against natural things, which is sickness. I decided that I want to come live here in the bush

(Govan) You guys’ patrol?
(Justin) Yes.
(Govan) And you say to the team, listen gents, see you later, I'm gonna go live with these rhinos.
(Justin) Yes. They thought I was crazy. They were looking at me like, okay, no, this guy is definitely nuts.

(Govan voice over) Four years ago, Justin filled a rucksack with rations, kissed his wife goodbye, and pitched a makeshift shelter right next to these rhinos.
(Justin up sound at the camp subtitles) It's a bit messy, but this is where I sleep. Okay, so nothing is super-neat yet. But here's the braai area. This is where we wash the dishes. Underneath, I keep me milk and cooldrink cold. Back there is the long drop. So, this is how I have it; the rhino camp is over there, and over here is where I store all my food items. And this is the kitchen with a gas stove.

(Govan voice over) For 8 months, he was isolated, determined to learn the rhinos’ rhythms and understand their language…. a connection crucial to getting close enough to protect them.
(Justin) At first, I was chased a lot. Because they are wild. I mean, that's what a rhino does. It is gonna happen because that’s their form of defending themselves. But I kept on going back.
(Justin up sound at the camp subtitles) Come! Go back! Oh, f*ck! Oh!

(Justin) The one time I was hitting my face and my back tooth got hit out, I use that as a learning opportunity Okay, I must put my hands in front of me. Every throne, every chase, I learned from that. With the one incident, she, in fact, hooked me on my bum and threw me, like, over two metres in the air

(Govan) Why would you go back to that, bro? How did you know that this was going to work?
(Justin) I didn't. I will be honest with you, I did not. I just kept on going, but their behavior started to change towards me. It's so difficult to explain this to someone, I could feel the energy that these riders, okay, they're not actually coming to hurt me now,
(Govan voice over) Justin did what few – if any – ever could; he was a part of the herd
(Govan) it kind of sounds like the stuff from the movies.But I suppose it's impossible to achieve that without some kind of sacrifice.

(Justin) Yeah, absolutely.
(Govan) So what did you lose?
(Justin) My relationship didn't work out anymore.
We started to drift apart. Because, what my ex-wife wanted in life it wasn't what I wanted.

(Govan) That's a heavy sacrifice to make for a rhino.
(Justin) If you want to live the life that you really want, you're going to have your challenges.

(Govan) What's the greatest moment of love you felt between you and your rhino?
(Justin) There was a small period, that I was alone here. I was overworked and I was extremely tired. I had this feeling of hopelessness in me.
I was just sitting there and THEN the rhinos came to my area. they came in a circle, like around me. I looked up and I looked behind me and they were just standing, They didn't try to do anything with their horn, try to push me They were just standing.
It's almost. Like THEY ARE sensing my like depression. They just looked at me almost like they are comforting me, like a hug. I realized that all this time I was here for them. And it's like they're showing. They are here for me too, because I needed them. I needed love in that moment because I was so alone.
(Member of the Anti-Poaching Unit briefing the team) We gonna take the poachers route, that is the easiest route between the road and the Rhino
(Govan) Justin, what’s the risk factor tonight
So, it is full moon tonight, so we have to be on high alert. It’s always on full moon that we have to be on high alert
(Govan voice over) By day, Justin may be bare-footed and carefree, But at night, he moves with purpose, heavily armed and alert, as part of a tight-knit anti-poaching team.
(Justin) Oscar one, behind
(Justin) From this point forward, we have to start talking very quietly to one another alright.

(Govan voice over) It was freezing. My feet were wet. And I kept thinking; how does he do this all night.
(Govan) Justin did you stay in the bush in these conditions?
(Justin) Yes, I did. It’s absolutely terrible.

(Justin) I'm the middleman between the rhino and the poacher. They have to get through me to get to the rhino. I will be willing to give my life for that. I can stop this. Maybe not for all the rhinos, but at least the ones that I protect.
(Govan voice over) We stayed on patrol with Justin and his team into the early hours of the morning, because the threat to these rhinos, the ones he calls family, is real. Every step he takes through the dark is a quiet promise: to keep them breathing till dawn.
(Justin) This sucks, I know people always think this is so cool. Walking around with a firearm. But no, once you gotta use this and really be out here for the duties, it's not so nice.
I really hope that there comes a point where we can put them back in the wild and they are just left alone.
I'll be happy to lay down my weapons and say we've done.
